properties.id: Paint the Future, Let Them Choose
properties.description: When difficult personnel decisions are needed, 'I just painted the picture that there is a future, and she's not part of it. I allowed her to think about it and come back.' This preserves dignity while achieving necessary outcomes.

Ensure difficult decisions appear to be the person's choice publicly - 'It was all publicly... It was all her decision. I was the only one who could make that happen. It was entirely my decision.' The benevolent dictator takes responsibility while preserving dignity.

When operations and HR conflict over discipline, act 'almost like a negotiator going back and forth between ops and HR. Both of them knew I could just make a decision to be done with it, but that's not how I wanted to do it. I just wanted to reach the best decision for the business.'
Handle necessary personnel removals by painting the future reality, allowing time for processing, and crafting solutions that preserve dignity while achieving business needs.
properties.context: Situations where valued but problematic employees need to be removed, particularly when they have personal circumstances requiring consideration.

properties.description: Use clear decision-making authority as background leverage while actively facilitating negotiation between conflicting parties to reach optimal business decisions.
properties.context: Interdepartmental conflicts where quick executive decisions are possible but collaborative solutions are preferable for long-term team dynamics.

properties.content: At the manufacturing company, a leadership team member 'had to go for a million reasons' but no one would make the decision. Dan 'painted the picture that there is a future, and she's not part of it' and allowed her to process. She ultimately chose announced retirement with continued health insurance for upcoming surgery. 'It was all her decision' publicly, though 'I was the only one who could make that happen.'

When operations and HR conflicted over disciplining a valuable but problematic sawmill worker in rural Indiana, Dan acted 'almost like a negotiator going back and forth' between them. Though 'both of them knew I could just make a decision to be done with it,' he facilitated a compromise solution (suspension while keeping employment) that served 'the best decision for the business.'

properties.description: 'I'm listening for resistance to whatever I'm saying' and determining 'whether that resistance is passing any logical test or whether it's pure emotion.' This applies equally to agreement: 'are you just agreeing with me on a logical side or on an emotional side?'
'I need to know that you're landing on the logic side. If I will probably dismiss what you have to say from the emotional side.' This represents a clear hierarchy of reasoning validity.
Actively assess whether responses (both resistance and agreement) are emotionally or logically driven, prioritizing logical reasoning while dismissing purely emotional responses.
properties.context: Business discussions where emotional reactions might cloud judgment or prevent optimal decision-making.

properties.description: Distinguish between resistance that 'is passing any logical test' versus 'pure emotion' to determine which objections deserve consideration and response.
properties.context: Change management or decision-making processes where pushback needs to be evaluated for its rational merit rather than dismissed automatically.

properties.id: Reading People - Logic vs Emotion Assessment
properties.content: When reading people as individuals beyond their roles, Dan focuses on 'listening for resistance to whatever I'm saying' and determining 'whether that resistance is passing any logical test or whether it's pure emotion.' The same applies to agreement - he needs to know people are 'landing on the logic side' because he will 'probably dismiss what you have to say from the emotional side.'

properties.description: 'I try to just put time on my side. I try not to... If I cannot deal with it at that time, I don't... Because I think that's really hard to move someone from one side to the other.' Avoids direct confrontation of emotion in the moment.

'I don't know that I ever confront the emotion directly.' Instead, uses phrases like 'Okay, let's just stop. I'm not going to make a decision right now. I hear what you're saying. Let me go back and see if we can get it resolved that way.'

With chronically emotional people, 'I gotta let that air out of the balloon because... Until he just obloviates whatever it is that he's doing... until he is finished bloviating, even though I'm not listening until he does that, he's not hearing me.'
After letting emotional people vent, 'I sort of go over back to the extreme on the other side and get really detailed on what I need and when I need it. It's almost like the counterbalance to that.'
When emotion arises, immediately pause the conversation, acknowledge what was heard, and postpone decision-making to allow emotional processing time.
properties.context: High-stakes business discussions where emotional responses threaten logical decision-making and immediate resolution isn't critical.

properties.id: Bloviation Tolerance followed by Extreme Precision
properties.description: Allow chronically emotional people to fully express themselves without listening engagement, then counterbalance with extremely detailed, specific requirements and timelines.
properties.context: Working with team members who have persistent emotional communication styles that disrupt logical discourse.

properties.content: When an typically logical HR person became emotional during a discipline discussion, Dan said 'Okay, let's just stop. I'm not going to make a decision right now. I hear what you're saying. Let me go back and see if we can get it resolved that way.' He notes 'I don't know that I ever confront the emotion directly.'

With a marketing team member who was chronically emotional, Dan realized 'I gotta let that air out of the balloon because... Until he just obloviates whatever it is that he's doing... until he is finished bloviating, even though I'm not listening until he does that, he's not hearing me.' His response was to 'go over back to the extreme on the other side and get really detailed on what I need and when I need it.'
